   143	 * payload, each tracked by its own [OptimisticWrite]; everything below says about [unitWrite] and
   144	 * [chooseUnit] holds unchanged for [viewWrite] and [chooseSessionView].

   146	 * The display-unit preference decides the unit a **newly created** workout is stamped with, and
   147	 * nothing else: it rewrites no stored weight, converts nothing, and is not consulted by a workout
   148	 * that already names a unit of its own. Writing it therefore invalidates no open screen — see
   149	 * [com.gymie.shared.ui.workout.WorkoutEditorState.open] for the rule that makes that true.
   150	 *
   151	 * ### Reads and writes are tracked on independent sequences, never one shared revision
   152	 *
   153	 * [load] answers "what does the server hold", [chooseUnit] answers "did the server accept what I
   154	 * just told it" — different questions. Conflating reads and writes into one shared revision counter
   155	 * (this class's original design) is what let a stale write's *failure* discard a fresher read's true
   156	 * answer, and separately let a stale read discard a fresher write's *confirmed success*. So each is
   157	 * tracked against its own sequence — [load] via [loadSeq], [chooseUnit] via [unitWrite]'s internal
   158	 * sequence — and the write keeps its own running count of the times it has actually *succeeded*
   159	 * ([OptimisticWrite.succeededWriteCount]) — not just the newest call, every one, because even a write
   160	 * whose own optimistic value later loses to a newer write still changed the server:

   163	 *   since superseded it — a write that later loses the screen to a newer one still changed the
   164	 *   server, and a later failure must revert to what it actually confirmed, not to a value the server
   165	 *   has since moved past. The visible [displayUnit] only follows along when its own write is still
   166	 *   the newest one — independent of any load, in flight or not — which is also what lets a write's
   167	 *   confirmed success stick on-screen even when an older, slower read resolves after it: the read is
   168	 *   not consulted at all here.
   169	 * - A **write**'s failure reverts [displayUnit] to its own confirmed value only when one exists.
   170	 *   Before anything has ever been confirmed there is nothing honest to revert to, so the control is
   171	 *   left showing the optimistic choice, the failure is still reported, and [loadFailed] is raised so
   172	 *   the screen offers the same retry path a failed [load] does — see [OptimisticWrite.onFailure].
   173	 * - A **load**'s success clears [loadFailed] only if it is still the newest load *and* no write has
   174	 *   succeeded since this load began — a write already answered the question this load was asking, so
   175	 *   a stale load's own answer is not news. [unitWrite]'s own confirmed/visible value updates
   176	 *   independently through [OptimisticWrite.adoptLoad], gated on no write having succeeded since; the
   177	 *   visible value additionally updates only while the write is not currently in flight, exactly as
   178	 *   [OptimisticWrite.adoptLoad] itself already enforces. A *stale* success (superseded load, or a
   179	 *   write has since succeeded) touches neither the confirmed nor visible value for the same reason a
   180	 *   stale write's own response is not adopted elsewhere: the write that made it moot already answered
   181	 *   the question.
   182	 * - A **load**'s failure is gated exactly the same way its success's [loadFailed] clearing is: only
   183	 *   while it is still the newest load *and* no write has succeeded since it began does it raise
   184	 *   [loadFailed] and report a failure. A write's success already answered the question this load was
   185	 *   asking, so a stale load's own failure to answer it is not news and must not undo that answer.
   186	 *
   187	 * [isLoading] and [isSaving] are reference counts — see their own docs — because [load] and
   188	 * [chooseUnit] can each be called again before an earlier call of the *same* function has answered:
   189	 * the screen launches a fresh coroutine per click, and [load] fires once at mount while the button is
   190	 * already interactive. [chooseUnit]'s network sends are additionally serialised through [sendMutex]
   191	 * so the server receives every write strictly in tap order.
   192	 *
   193	 * [isLoading], [isSaving] and [loadFailed] exist only so the screen can show progress and, after a
   194	 * failed [load] (or a failed write with nothing yet confirmed), an in-place retry — none of the three
   195	 * ever decides what [displayUnit] shows on its own.
   196	 *
   197	 * It takes [WorkoutCatalogApi] rather than the whole client because the preferences are the only
   198	 * thing it touches; nothing here can reach a workout.
   199	 */
   200	class SettingsState(
   201	    private val api: WorkoutCatalogApi,
   202	    private val notifications: NotificationState,
   203	) {
   204	    /** Backs [displayUnit] and everything [load]/[chooseUnit] track about it. */
   205	    private val unitWrite = OptimisticWrite(WeightUnit.KG)
   206	
   207	    /** What the control shows. Kilograms until [load] has answered, matching the server's default. */
   208	    val displayUnit: WeightUnit
   209	        get() = unitWrite.value
   210	
   211	    /** Backs [sessionView] and everything [load]/[chooseSessionView] track about it. */
   212	    private val viewWrite = OptimisticWrite(SessionView.FOCUS)
   213	
   214	    /** What the workout-mode control shows. Focus until [load] has answered, matching the server's default. */
   215	    val sessionView: SessionView
   216	        get() = viewWrite.value
   217	
   218	    /** How many [load] calls are currently in flight; [isLoading] is true while this is positive. */
   219	    private var loadingCalls: Int by mutableStateOf(0)
   220	
   221	    /** True from the moment any [load] call starts until every overlapping one has answered. */
   222	    val isLoading: Boolean
   223	        get() = loadingCalls > 0
   224	
   225	    /**
   226	     * False until [load] has answered once, success or failure. The screen draws a skeleton until then:
   227	     * [displayUnit] reads kilograms before the answer, and a user on pounds saw it flip (KAN-575 fix
   228	     * round 4).
   229	     */
   230	    var hasLoaded: Boolean by mutableStateOf(false)
   231	        private set
   232	
   233	    /** True while at least one [chooseUnit] or [chooseSessionView] call is in flight. */
   234	    val isSaving: Boolean
   235	        get() = unitWrite.isSaving || viewWrite.isSaving
   236	
   237	    /**
   238	     * True once the latest [load] has failed, or the latest [chooseUnit] failed with nothing yet
   239	     * confirmed to fall back on — either way the screen offers the same in-place retry, which is just
   240	     * [load] again.
   241	     */
   242	    var loadFailed: Boolean by mutableStateOf(false)
   243	        private set
   244	
   245	    /** Advanced by every [load] call; a response is applied only while it is still the newest one. */
   246	    private val loadSeq = Sequencer()
   247	
   248	    /** Serialises every [chooseUnit] and [chooseSessionView] send — see the class KDoc. */
   249	    private val sendMutex = Mutex()
   250	
   251	    /** Reads the stored preferences, so the control opens on what the server actually holds. */
   252	    suspend fun load() {
   253	        val thisLoadSeq = loadSeq.next()
   254	        val unitWritesBeforeThisLoad = unitWrite.succeededWriteCount
   255	        val viewWritesBeforeThisLoad = viewWrite.succeededWriteCount
   256	        loadingCalls++
   257	        try {
   258	            val result = runCatching { api.getPreferences() }
   259	            // Computed once, right after the suspending call above returns and before either branch
   260	            // below runs — there is no suspension point in between, so this cannot go stale by the
   261	            // time either branch reads it. A write that succeeded after this load began already told
   262	            // us the truth about the server, so this load's own answer — success *or* failure — is
   263	            // stale and must not be treated as new information.
   264	            val noUnitWriteSucceededSinceThisLoadBegan = unitWrite.succeededWriteCount == unitWritesBeforeThisLoad
   265	            val noViewWriteSucceededSinceThisLoadBegan = viewWrite.succeededWriteCount == viewWritesBeforeThisLoad
   266	            val current = loadSeq.isCurrent(thisLoadSeq)
   267	            val noWriteSucceeded = noUnitWriteSucceededSinceThisLoadBegan && noViewWriteSucceededSinceThisLoadBegan
   268	            result
   269	                .onSuccess {
   270	                    if (current && noWriteSucceeded) loadFailed = false
   271	                    if (current && noUnitWriteSucceededSinceThisLoadBegan) unitWrite.adoptLoad(it.displayUnit)
   272	                    if (current && noViewWriteSucceededSinceThisLoadBegan) viewWrite.adoptLoad(it.sessionView)
   273	                }.onFailureNotCancelled {
   274	                    if (current && noWriteSucceeded) {
   275	                        loadFailed = true
   276	                        notifications.failure(it.message ?: "Could not load your settings.")
   277	                    }
   278	                }
   279	        } finally {
   280	            loadingCalls--
   281	            hasLoaded = true
   282	        }
   283	    }
   284	
   285	    /**
   286	     * Stores [unit] as the display preference, adopting whatever the server answers is now in
   287	     * force, and putting the control back to its last confirmed value if the write is refused — see
   288	     * the class KDoc for exactly when each of those happens.
   289	     */
   290	    suspend fun chooseUnit(unit: WeightUnit) {
   291	        val token = unitWrite.begin(unit)
   292	        try {
   293	            runCatching { sendMutex.withLock { api.updatePreferences(displayUnit = unit) } }
   294	                .onSuccess {
   295	                    if (unitWrite.onSuccess(token, it.displayUnit)) loadFailed = false
   296	                }.onFailureNotCancelled {
   297	                    when (unitWrite.onFailure(token)) {
   298	                        WriteFailureOutcome.STALE -> {
   299	                            Unit
   300	                        }
   301	
   302	                        WriteFailureOutcome.REVERTED_TO_CONFIRMED -> {
   303	                            notifications.failure(it.message ?: "Could not save your weight unit.")
   304	                        }
   305	
   306	                        WriteFailureOutcome.NOTHING_CONFIRMED -> {
   307	                            // Nothing has ever been confirmed: reverting would invent a value the
   308	                            // server never sent. Leave the control where it is and offer the same
   309	                            // retry path a failed load does, so the user can re-sync.
   310	                            loadFailed = true
   311	                            notifications.failure(it.message ?: "Could not save your weight unit.")
   312	                        }
   313	                    }
   314	                }
   315	        } finally {
   316	            unitWrite.end()
   317	        }
   318	    }
   319	
   320	    /**
   321	     * Stores [view] as the workout mode, exactly as [chooseUnit] stores the unit. The backend requires
   322	     * `displayUnit` on every PUT, so this write carries the unit's last confirmed value — read inside
   323	     * [sendMutex], once every earlier write has settled, so a unit choice still queued behind this
   324	     * one never reaches the server through it. With nothing confirmed (a failed [load]) nothing is
   325	     * sent: the write fails like a refused one. The answer's unit is not adopted: the unit's own
   326	     * writes and loads own that field.
   327	     */
   328	    suspend fun chooseSessionView(view: SessionView) {
   329	        val token = viewWrite.begin(view)
   330	        try {
   331	            runCatching {
   332	                sendMutex.withLock {
   333	                    // No confirmed unit (the load failed) means no honest value to send: the default
   334	                    // would overwrite a stored LBS with KG. Refuse, and let the retry path re-sync.
   335	                    val unit = unitWrite.confirmed ?: error("Could not save your workout mode.")
   336	                    api.updatePreferences(displayUnit = unit, sessionView = view)
   337	                }
   338	            }.onSuccess {
   339	                if (viewWrite.onSuccess(token, it.sessionView)) loadFailed = false
   340	            }.onFailureNotCancelled {
   341	                when (viewWrite.onFailure(token)) {
   342	                    WriteFailureOutcome.STALE -> {
   343	                        Unit
   344	                    }
   345	
   346	                    WriteFailureOutcome.REVERTED_TO_CONFIRMED -> {
   347	                        notifications.failure(it.message ?: "Could not save your workout mode.")
   348	                    }
   349	
   350	                    WriteFailureOutcome.NOTHING_CONFIRMED -> {
   351	                        loadFailed = true
   352	                        notifications.failure(it.message ?: "Could not save your workout mode.")
   353	                    }
   354	                }
   355	            }
   356	        } finally {
   357	            viewWrite.end()
   358	        }
   359	    }
   360	}

   130	     * field is currently in flight — a pending optimistic choice must not be clobbered by a read
   131	     * that was already stale the moment it was issued, even when that read's answer is still good
   132	     * enough to become the new confirmed value.

   136	        if (!isSaving) value = serverValue
   137	    }

   140	/**
   141	 * Plain Kotlin state holder (no `@Composable` in its API) behind the Settings screen's display-unit
   142	 * control and its workout-mode control ([sessionView], KAN-867) — two fields of one preferences
   143	 * payload, each tracked by its own [OptimisticWrite]; everything below says about [unitWrite] and
   144	 * [chooseUnit] holds unchanged for [viewWrite] and [chooseSessionView].
   145	 *
   146	 * The display-unit preference decides the unit a **newly created** workout is stamped with, and
   147	 * nothing else: it rewrites no stored weight, converts nothing, and is not consulted by a workout
   148	 * that already names a unit of its own. Writing it therefore invalidates no open screen — see
   149	 * [com.gymie.shared.ui.workout.WorkoutEditorState.open] for the rule that makes that true.
   150	 *
   151	 * ### Reads and writes are tracked on independent sequences, never one shared revision
   152	 *
   153	 * [load] answers "what does the server hold", [chooseUnit] answers "did the server accept what I
   154	 * just told it" — different questions. Conflating reads and writes into one shared revision counter
   155	 * (this class's original design) is what let a stale write's *failure* discard a fresher read's true
   156	 * answer, and separately let a stale read discard a fresher write's *confirmed success*. So each is
   157	 * tracked against its own sequence — [load] via [loadSeq], [chooseUnit] via [unitWrite]'s internal
   158	 * sequence — and the write keeps its own running count of the times it has actually *succeeded*
   159	 * ([OptimisticWrite.succeededWriteCount]) — not just the newest call, every one, because even a write
   160	 * whose own optimistic value later loses to a newer write still changed the server:
   161	 *
   162	 * - A **write**'s success always updates [unitWrite]'s confirmed value, even when a newer write has
   163	 *   since superseded it — a write that later loses the screen to a newer one still changed the
   164	 *   server, and a later failure must revert to what it actually confirmed, not to a value the server
   165	 *   has since moved past. The visible [displayUnit] only follows along when its own write is still
   166	 *   the newest one — independent of any load, in flight or not — which is also what lets a write's
   167	 *   confirmed success stick on-screen even when an older, slower read resolves after it: the read is
   168	 *   not consulted at all here.
   169	 * - A **write**'s failure reverts [displayUnit] to its own confirmed value only when one exists.
   170	 *   Before anything has ever been confirmed there is nothing honest to revert to, so the control is
   171	 *   left showing the optimistic choice, the failure is still reported, and [loadFailed] is raised so
   172	 *   the screen offers the same retry path a failed [load] does — see [OptimisticWrite.onFailure].
   173	 * - A **load**'s success clears [loadFailed] only if it is still the newest load *and* no write has
   174	 *   succeeded since this load began — a write already answered the question this load was asking, so
   175	 *   a stale load's own answer is not news. [unitWrite]'s own confirmed/visible value updates
   176	 *   independently through [OptimisticWrite.adoptLoad], gated on no write having succeeded since; the
   177	 *   visible value additionally updates only while the write is not currently in flight, exactly as
   178	 *   [OptimisticWrite.adoptLoad] itself already enforces. A *stale* success (superseded load, or a
   179	 *   write has since succeeded) touches neither the confirmed nor visible value for the same reason a
   180	 *   stale write's own response is not adopted elsewhere: the write that made it moot already answered
   181	 *   the question.
   182	 * - A **load**'s failure is gated exactly the same way its success's [loadFailed] clearing is: only
   183	 *   while it is still the newest load *and* no write has succeeded since it began does it raise
   184	 *   [loadFailed] and report a failure. A write's success already answered the question this load was
   185	 *   asking, so a stale load's own failure to answer it is not news and must not undo that answer.
   186	 *
   187	 * [isLoading] and [isSaving] are reference counts — see their own docs — because [load] and
   188	 * [chooseUnit] can each be called again before an earlier call of the *same* function has answered:
   189	 * the screen launches a fresh coroutine per click, and [load] fires once at mount while the button is
   190	 * already interactive. [chooseUnit]'s network sends are additionally serialised through [sendMutex]
   191	 * so the server receives every write strictly in tap order.

   193	 * [isLoading], [isSaving] and [loadFailed] exist only so the screen can show progress and, after a
   194	 * failed [load] (or a failed write with nothing yet confirmed), an in-place retry — none of the three
   195	 * ever decides what [displayUnit] shows on its own.
   196	 *
   197	 * It takes [WorkoutCatalogApi] rather than the whole client because the preferences are the only
   198	 * thing it touches; nothing here can reach a workout.
   199	 */

   201	    private val api: WorkoutCatalogApi,
   202	    private val notifications: NotificationState,
   203	) {
   204	    /** Backs [displayUnit] and everything [load]/[chooseUnit] track about it. */
   205	    private val unitWrite = OptimisticWrite(WeightUnit.KG)
   206	
   207	    /** What the control shows. Kilograms until [load] has answered, matching the server's default. */
   208	    val displayUnit: WeightUnit
   209	        get() = unitWrite.value
   210	
   211	    /** Backs [sessionView] and everything [load]/[chooseSessionView] track about it. */
   212	    private val viewWrite = OptimisticWrite(SessionView.FOCUS)
   213	
   214	    /** What the workout-mode control shows. Focus until [load] has answered, matching the server's default. */
   215	    val sessionView: SessionView
   216	        get() = viewWrite.value
   217	
   218	    /** How many [load] calls are currently in flight; [isLoading] is true while this is positive. */
   219	    private var loadingCalls: Int by mutableStateOf(0)
   220	
   221	    /** True from the moment any [load] call starts until every overlapping one has answered. */
   222	    val isLoading: Boolean
   223	        get() = loadingCalls > 0
   224	
   225	    /**

   227	     * [displayUnit] reads kilograms before the answer, and a user on pounds saw it flip (KAN-575 fix
   228	     * round 4).
   229	     */
   230	    var hasLoaded: Boolean by mutableStateOf(false)
   231	        private set
   232	
   233	    /** True while at least one [chooseUnit] or [chooseSessionView] call is in flight. */
   234	    val isSaving: Boolean
   235	        get() = unitWrite.isSaving || viewWrite.isSaving
   236	
   237	    /**
   238	     * True once the latest [load] has failed, or the latest [chooseUnit] failed with nothing yet
   239	     * confirmed to fall back on — either way the screen offers the same in-place retry, which is just
   240	     * [load] again.
   241	     */
   242	    var loadFailed: Boolean by mutableStateOf(false)
   243	        private set
   244	
   245	    /** Advanced by every [load] call; a response is applied only while it is still the newest one. */
   246	    private val loadSeq = Sequencer()
   247	
   248	    /** Serialises every [chooseUnit] and [chooseSessionView] send — see the class KDoc. */
   249	    private val sendMutex = Mutex()
   250	
   251	    /** Reads the stored preferences, so the control opens on what the server actually holds. */
   252	    suspend fun load() {
   253	        val thisLoadSeq = loadSeq.next()
   254	        val unitWritesBeforeThisLoad = unitWrite.succeededWriteCount
   255	        val viewWritesBeforeThisLoad = viewWrite.succeededWriteCount
   256	        loadingCalls++
   257	        try {
   258	            val result = runCatching { api.getPreferences() }
   259	            // Computed once, right after the suspending call above returns and before either branch
   260	            // below runs — there is no suspension point in between, so this cannot go stale by the
   261	            // time either branch reads it. A write that succeeded after this load began already told
   262	            // us the truth about the server, so this load's own answer — success *or* failure — is
   263	            // stale and must not be treated as new information.
   264	            val noUnitWriteSucceededSinceThisLoadBegan = unitWrite.succeededWriteCount == unitWritesBeforeThisLoad
   265	            val noViewWriteSucceededSinceThisLoadBegan = viewWrite.succeededWriteCount == viewWritesBeforeThisLoad
   266	            val current = loadSeq.isCurrent(thisLoadSeq)
   267	            val noWriteSucceeded = noUnitWriteSucceededSinceThisLoadBegan && noViewWriteSucceededSinceThisLoadBegan
   268	            result
   269	                .onSuccess {
   270	                    if (current && noWriteSucceeded) loadFailed = false
   271	                    if (current && noUnitWriteSucceededSinceThisLoadBegan) unitWrite.adoptLoad(it.displayUnit)
   272	                    if (current && noViewWriteSucceededSinceThisLoadBegan) viewWrite.adoptLoad(it.sessionView)
   273	                }.onFailureNotCancelled {
   274	                    if (current && noWriteSucceeded) {
   275	                        loadFailed = true
   276	                        notifications.failure(it.message ?: "Could not load your settings.")
   277	                    }
   278	                }
   279	        } finally {
   280	            loadingCalls--
   281	            hasLoaded = true
   282	        }
   283	    }
   284	
   285	    /**
   286	     * Stores [unit] as the display preference, adopting whatever the server answers is now in
   287	     * force, and putting the control back to its last confirmed value if the write is refused — see
   288	     * the class KDoc for exactly when each of those happens.
   289	     */
   290	    suspend fun chooseUnit(unit: WeightUnit) {
   291	        val token = unitWrite.begin(unit)
   292	        try {
   293	            runCatching { sendMutex.withLock { api.updatePreferences(displayUnit = unit) } }
   294	                .onSuccess {
   295	                    if (unitWrite.onSuccess(token, it.displayUnit)) loadFailed = false
   296	                }.onFailureNotCancelled {
   297	                    when (unitWrite.onFailure(token)) {
   298	                        WriteFailureOutcome.STALE -> {
   299	                            Unit
   300	                        }
   301	
   302	                        WriteFailureOutcome.REVERTED_TO_CONFIRMED -> {
   303	                            notifications.failure(it.message ?: "Could not save your weight unit.")
   304	                        }
   305	
   306	                        WriteFailureOutcome.NOTHING_CONFIRMED -> {
   307	                            // Nothing has ever been confirmed: reverting would invent a value the
   308	                            // server never sent. Leave the control where it is and offer the same
   309	                            // retry path a failed load does, so the user can re-sync.
   310	                            loadFailed = true
   311	                            notifications.failure(it.message ?: "Could not save your weight unit.")
   312	                        }
   313	                    }
   314	                }
   315	        } finally {
   316	            unitWrite.end()
   317	        }
   318	    }
   319	
   320	    /**
   321	     * Stores [view] as the workout mode, exactly as [chooseUnit] stores the unit. The backend requires
   322	     * `displayUnit` on every PUT, so this write carries the unit's last confirmed value — read inside
   323	     * [sendMutex], once every earlier write has settled, so a unit choice still queued behind this
   324	     * one never reaches the server through it. With nothing confirmed (a failed [load]) nothing is
   325	     * sent: the write fails like a refused one. The answer's unit is not adopted: the unit's own
   326	     * writes and loads own that field.
   327	     */
   328	    suspend fun chooseSessionView(view: SessionView) {
   329	        val token = viewWrite.begin(view)
   330	        try {
   331	            runCatching {
   332	                sendMutex.withLock {
   333	                    // No confirmed unit (the load failed) means no honest value to send: the default
   334	                    // would overwrite a stored LBS with KG. Refuse, and let the retry path re-sync.
   335	                    val unit = unitWrite.confirmed ?: error("Could not save your workout mode.")

   337	                }
   338	            }.onSuccess {
   339	                if (viewWrite.onSuccess(token, it.sessionView)) loadFailed = false
   340	            }.onFailureNotCancelled {
   341	                when (viewWrite.onFailure(token)) {
   342	                    WriteFailureOutcome.STALE -> {
   343	                        Unit
   344	                    }
   345	
   346	                    WriteFailureOutcome.REVERTED_TO_CONFIRMED -> {
   347	                        notifications.failure(it.message ?: "Could not save your workout mode.")
   348	                    }
   349	
   350	                    WriteFailureOutcome.NOTHING_CONFIRMED -> {
   351	                        loadFailed = true
   352	                        notifications.failure(it.message ?: "Could not save your workout mode.")
   353	                    }
   354	                }
   355	            }
   356	        } finally {
   357	            viewWrite.end()
   358	        }
   359	    }
   360	}

## Review of KAN-867: the Workout mode setting

I couldn't find any plan files for KAN-867 under `openspec/`, `spectre/` or `docs/`. So I checked the diff against the claims made in its own comments and docs, not against a plan. I didn't run Gradle; every point below comes from reading the code. The diff contains nothing that tries to give the reviewer instructions.

### Shared-state check

Existing state that the new code reads or writes: `loadFailed`, `sendMutex`, `unitWrite.confirmed`, `unitWrite.succeededWriteCount`, `loadSeq`, `hasLoaded`, `isSaving`.

**`loadFailed`** used to mean "the unit has no confirmed value". It now also has to mean "the workout mode has no confirmed value". Every line that writes it:
- `SettingsState.kt:270` (a load succeeds and no write succeeded meanwhile): still correct. Both fields are adopted together on lines 271–272.
- `SettingsState.kt:275` (a load fails and no write succeeded meanwhile): still correct.
- `SettingsState.kt:295` (a unit write succeeds): **broken by this diff.** It clears the flag just because the unit is now confirmed, even when the workout mode never was. See Important #1.
- `SettingsState.kt:310` (a unit write fails with nothing confirmed): still correct.
- `SettingsState.kt:339` (a mode write succeeds): still correct. A mode write can only be sent once the unit is confirmed (line 335), so both fields are confirmed after it.
- `SettingsState.kt:351` (a mode write fails with nothing confirmed): still correct.

**The other state:**
- **`sendMutex`:** its only users are `:293` and `:332`, and both take the lock. Still correct.
- **`unitWrite.confirmed`:** it is only written inside `OptimisticWrite.onSuccess` (`:103`) and `adoptLoad` (`:135`). The diff reads it inside the lock (`:335`), after every earlier send has settled. Still correct.
- **`unitWrite.succeededWriteCount`:** only written at `:102`. The load gating at `:264–272` now gates each field separately. Still correct.
- **`loadSeq`:** only written at `:253`. Still correct.
- **`hasLoaded`:** only written at `:281`. The new row is drawn inside its gate (`AppScreens.kt:221`). Still correct.
- **`isSaving`:** it is now computed from both writes (`:235`) and nothing in the UI reads `SettingsState.isSaving`. Still correct.

### Issues

#### Critical (Must Fix)
None.

#### Important (Should Fix)

**1. A successful unit save after a failed load hides Retry while the Workout mode row shows an unconfirmed Focus.**
- **Where:** `shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/com/gymie/shared/ui/SettingsState.kt:295`
- **What happens:**
  1. The first load fails, so `loadFailed` is true and `viewWrite.confirmed` is null. The screen still draws all rows, because `hasLoaded` becomes true on failure too.
  2. The user taps LBS and the save succeeds.
  3. Line 295 clears `loadFailed`, so the Retry button (`AppScreens.kt:326`) disappears.
  4. The Workout mode row keeps showing the default `FOCUS`, which the server never confirmed. A user whose stored mode is QUICK now sees Focus with no way to re-sync.
- **Why it's a defect:** the row's own doc (`AppScreens.kt:393`) promises it is "never a default Focus". Also, the response to the unit save already contains the server's real `sessionView`, and it is thrown away.
- **How to fix:** in `chooseUnit`'s `onSuccess`, adopt `it.sessionView` into `viewWrite` the same way a load does (only while no mode write is in flight or has succeeded since). Or, at minimum, clear `loadFailed` only when `viewWrite.confirmed != null`. Add a test for this sequence next to `a write that succeeds clears a retry offer…` (`SettingsStateTest.kt:435`), which currently locks in the old behaviour that only considered the unit.
- **Reproducer:** none. It needs a new test in `SettingsStateTest`:
  - set `preferencesResult` to a failure and call `load()`
  - set `preferencesResult` to `success(KG, QUICK)`
  - call `chooseUnit(LBS)`
  - assert `loadFailed || sessionView == QUICK`

  Today that assertion fails: `loadFailed` is false and `sessionView` is `FOCUS`.

#### Minor (Nice to Have)

**2. Some docs are out of date.**
- **Where:** `SettingsState.kt:237-240` and `:143-144`
- **What's wrong:** the `loadFailed` doc still mentions only `chooseUnit`. The class doc says everything about `unitWrite` "holds unchanged" for `viewWrite`, but the mode write has its own refuse-without-a-confirmed-unit path and shares `loadFailed` across both fields.
- **Why it matters:** these are exactly the rules Important #1 got wrong.
- **Reproducer:** none — documentation only.

**3. The Retry button sits under the wrong row after a failed mode write.**
- **Where:** `AppScreens.kt:326`
- **What's wrong:** when a mode write fails with nothing confirmed, the Retry it raises appears under the Weight unit row, with the tag `settings_display_unit_retry`, two rows away from the control the user just tapped.
- **Reproducer:** none — layout and UX.

**4. Older servers will silently undo a Quick choice.**
- **Where:** `WorkoutModels.kt:697`
- **What's wrong:** if the client ships before the backend returns `sessionView`, the response omits the field and it decodes as `FOCUS`. `viewWrite.onSuccess` then adopts `FOCUS`, so choosing Quick snaps back to Focus with no error shown.
- **Why it matters:** the backend isn't in this repo, so I can't check the deploy order. The PR should state which side ships first.
- **Reproducer:** none — depends on the backend.

**5. One new test has no feature tag.** `theWorkoutModeControlKeepsOneLineAtPhoneWidth` (`SettingsScreenUiTest.kt`) has no `@Feature`, unlike the other new tests.
- **Reproducer:** none — traceability only.

### Recommendations
- Treat `loadFailed` as "some field has no confirmed value", for example `unitWrite.confirmed == null || viewWrite.confirmed == null` combined with the load-failed flag. Then no single writer has to think about the other field.
- Have every successful PUT feed both fields from the response, since the server returns the whole preferences object. That fixes #1 and keeps the two fields in step.
- The new tests mostly exercise real behaviour: a fake that keeps state, and a `MockEngine` that inspects the actual JSON body. The rule that sends the confirmed unit and never one still queued is well covered.

### Assessment
**Ready for the human gate?** With fixes

**Reasoning:** The new mode write, the encoding of the field and the ordering under the shared lock are all sound. But the unit-save success path, which this diff didn't touch, now clears the shared retry flag while the workout mode is still unconfirmed. After a failed load that leaves a stale Focus on screen with no Retry.
